Easy Spinach Feta Egg White Wraps (Trader Joe’s Version)

ByAmee Livingston September 14, 2026September 14, 2026

If you love Starbucks’ spinach feta & egg white wrap but want to make it budget-friendly and from scratch, this recipe is about to become your new breakfast meal prep staple. It’s made almost entirely with Trader Joe’s ingredients, swaps in whole-wheat lavash for the wrap, and bakes the egg whites in a single batch for fast, easy prep. This version has the same amount of protein but fewer calories and carbs, and is just as good, if not better, than the original.

My daughter originally found a version of this in a meal prep ebook, and after a few tweaks to suit our taste, it’s been on repeat in our house ever since. One batch sets you up with breakfast for most of the week.

Why We Love It

  • Meal prep MVP. One sheet of baked eggs turns into six wraps you can grab straight from the fridge all week.
  • High protein, low effort. Liquid egg whites and feta boost the protein without the extra hands-on time of individual omelets.
  • Budget-friendly Starbucks swap. Trader Joe’s ingredients make this a fraction of the cost of the coffee shop version, and you can make a whole week’s worth for less than it would cost for a couple of store-bought wraps.
  • Freezer-friendly. Make a double batch and stash extras in the freezer for mornings when even reheating feels like too much.
  • Easy to customize. Swap in your favorite cheese, greens, or add-ins once you’ve got the base method down.

Ingredients

You’ll find every one of these at Trader Joe’s, but any brand will work if you’re shopping elsewhere.

  • Liquid egg whites – The base of the bake. Using liquid egg whites (rather than separating whole eggs) keeps things quick and mess-free.
  • Garlic powder – Whisked right into the egg whites for flavor in every bite.
  • Baby spinach – Roughly chopped so it distributes evenly through the eggs.
  • Sun-dried tomatoes in oil – Adds richness and a concentrated, slightly sweet tomato flavor.
  • Optional: Julienned sun-dried tomatoes (not in oil) – You can use these to lower the fat and calories, but they don’t have as much flavor. Sometimes I do 1/2 and 1/2, but the oil-based ones definitely taste the best.
  • Crumbled feta – Salty and tangy; it’s the ingredient that makes this taste like the Starbucks original.
  • Salt and pepper – To season the eggs to taste.
  • Light cream cheese – Spread on the lavash for creaminess and to help everything hold together. Feel free to add more, if desired.
  • Whole wheat lavash flatbreads – A sturdier, higher-fiber swap for a traditional wrap. Trader Joe’s lavash comes pre-scored down the middle, which makes portioning the wraps easy.

How to Make It

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a 9×13-inch baking dish with parchment paper, letting it come up the sides for easy removal later. Spritz the parchment with cooking spray and set the dish aside.
  2. Whisk the egg whites with the garlic powder, then pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
  3. Top evenly with the chopped fresh spinach, sun-dried tomatoes, feta, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
  4. Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the eggs are fully set. Let the egg bake cool completely before assembling the wraps — this makes it much easier to slice and roll.
  5. Once cooled, lift the egg bake out of the pan using the parchment and remove the parchment. Cut in half lengthwise, then cut each half into thirds, for 6 even egg slices.
  6. Split each lavash in half (Trader Joe’s lavash is pre-perforated for easy splitting). Spread a thin layer of light cream cheese on each half, then place one egg slice in the center.
  7. Fold one side of the lavash over the egg, then roll it up burrito-style. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap or foil.

Storing and Freezing

To store: Keep the wrapped wraps in the refrigerator for 3- 4 days. They’re ready to grab and reheat whenever you need breakfast.

To freeze: Wrap each one tightly in plastic wrap or foil, then place in a freezer-safe bag or container. They’ll keep well in the freezer for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating, or reheat straight from frozen and add a few extra minutes.

How to reheat:

  • Skillet (recommended): Heat a dry, nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Place the wrap in the skillet, and toast for about 2-3 minutes per side, until warmed through. The dry skillet with a cover gives you the best texture — a slightly crisp outside with a warmed-through center — without drying out the eggs.
  • Microwave: Heat for 30-45 seconds. This is the fastest option, but the skillet method is recommended for the best texture.
  • Air Fryer: You can cook these straight from the freezer in the air fryer. Preheat the air fryer to 350 degrees F. When heated, air fry the frozen wrap for 10-12 minutes until heated through. If not frozen, cook them for 5-6 minutes to crisp the flatbread.

FAQ

Can I use whole eggs instead of liquid egg whites?

You can, though the texture and protein content will change. If you swap in whole eggs, you’ll likely need fewer of them by volume, so start with less than the amount of liquid egg whites called for and adjust to fill the pan in a similar thin layer.

What can I use instead of lavash?

Any large, thin wrap or tortilla will work if you can’t find lavash. Just keep in mind that lavash is thinner and sturdier than a standard tortilla, so a flour tortilla wrap may roll up a little differently.

Can I add other vegetables?

Definitely. Mushrooms, bell peppers, or diced onion would all work well folded into the egg mixture before baking. Just make sure any watery vegetables are cooked down first so the eggs stay set.

Is this recipe freezer-friendly?

Yes, these wraps freeze well for up to 2 months. See the Storing and Freezing section above for full instructions.

Recipe tips

  • Amazon has 9×13 pan parchment liners that are great for lining the baking dish if you don’t mind spending a little extra for convenience. I use a glass baking pan, but metal works too.
  • I highly recommend toasting the wraps in a dry non-stick skillet or cast-iron skillet for the best texture.
  • These are best consumed within 3-4 days, or they will start to get soggy in the fridge.

Spinach Feta Egg White Wraps

The easiest breakfast meal prep made with baked egg whites, spinach, feta, and sun-dried tomatoes rolled in whole-wheat lavash. Freezer-friendly too.
No ratings yet
Print Pin Rate
Course: Breakfast
Cuisine: American
Prep Time: 10 minutes minutes
Cook Time: 25 minutes minutes
Total Time: 35 minutes minutes
Servings: 6 wraps
Calories: 244kcal
Author: Amee

Equipment

  • 9×13 baking dish
  • Parchment paper

Ingredients

  • 2½ cups liquid egg whites (600g)
  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 cup baby spinach (30g)
  • ½ cup sundried tomatoes in olive oil (45g)
  • ¾ cup crumbled feta cheese (113g)
  • ½ tsp salt
  • ¼ tsp pepper
  • 6 tbsp light cream cheese (90g)
  • 3 whole-wheat lavash flatbreads (108g)
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions

  • Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. and line a 9×13 baking dish with parchment paper, making sure it comes up the sides. Spritz with cooking spray and set aside. 
  • Whisk the egg whites with the garlic powder and pour them into the pan. 
  • Top with chopped spinach, sundried tomatoes, feta, and salt and pepper. 
  • Bake for 20-25 minutes until the eggs are set. Cool completely before assembling the wraps. 
  • When the egg bake has completely cooled, remove the parchment from the pan. Cut in half lengthwise, then into 3rds making 6 even slices. 
  • Spread the cream cheese on each lavash half (the Trader Joe's ones are already perforated for easy spliting. Then place an egg slice in the middle. 
  • Fold one side over the egg, then roll it up like a burrito. Wrap in plastic wrap or foil and refrigerate until ready to eat for up to 4 days.
  • To reheat: Heat a non-stick skillet over medium- medium-high heat and toast about 2-3 minutes per side. You can also microwave them for 30-45 seconds.

Notes

  • Amazon has 9×13 pan parchment liners that are great for lining the baking dish if you don’t mind spending a little extra for convenience. I use a glass baking pan, but metal works too.
  • I highly recommend toasting the wraps in a dry non-stick skillet or cast-iron skillet for the best texture. 
  • These are best consumed within 3-4 days, or they will start to get soggy in the fridge.
  • You can cook these straight from the freezer in the air fryer. Preheat the air fryer to 350 degrees F. When heated, air fry the frozen wrap for 10-12 minutes until heated through. If not frozen, cook them for 5-6 minutes to crisp the flatbread.
